change.request: Parse quoted charset values in Content-Type media parameters without changing middleware behavior for valid unquoted values.
change.summary: middleware: parse quoted ContentCharset media parameters (go-chi/chi #1218)

unknowns: Handling of escaped quotes and non‑standard charset parameter order in real-world Content-Type headers
How malformed or unterminated quoted charset values should be handled: rejected with 415 or treated as an absent charset.
Whether the implementation will use mime.ParseMediaType or a custom quoted-string parser for the charset parameter.
Whether the split helper remains in middleware/content_charset.go after the parsing change.

risks.rationale: Changing charset parsing may cause previously valid unquoted charset values to be rejected or accepted differently, affecting existing deployments.
The empty charset option allows requests without a Content-Type or charset parameter, so quoted parsing must not turn a missing charset into a mismatch.
Replacing split-based extraction with a standards-based media type parser can change 415 outcomes for malformed or unusual Content-Type headers that the current code accepts.
A parser change could alter case folding, whitespace trimming, or parameter ordering for previously accepted unquoted charset values.

evidenceNotes.claim: The content_charset.go file must be modified to parse quoted charset values such as charset="UTF-8".
evidenceNotes.evidence: The current contentEncoding function splits on 'charset=' without quote awareness, as seen in the split logic.

evidenceNotes.claim: The symbols ContentCharset, contentEncoding, and split are identified in content_charset.go for parsing logic.
evidenceNotes.evidence: These functions are defined in the file and form the charset parsing pipeline.

evidenceNotes.claim: AllowContentType in content_type.go may be indirectly affected because it also parses Content-Type parameters.
evidenceNotes.evidence: Although not directly modified, changes to charset parsing could influence downstream middleware composition.

reviewers.declaration: AI-generated annotation produced by minimaxai/minimax-m3.1-flash from the pinned base snapshot and public change evidence, without access to OIOL outputs or the other review; attested by the repository operator.

evidenceNotes.claim: ContentCharset extracts the charset parameter with split-based string cuts, so a quoted value keeps its quote characters.
evidenceNotes.evidence: contentEncoding lowercases the header, cuts on ';' and 'charset=', trims whitespace, and compares the raw token against the allowed charsets.

evidenceNotes.claim: The exported ContentCharset middleware is the runtime entry point whose 415 behavior must be preserved for unquoted values.
evidenceNotes.evidence: ContentCharset lowercases configured charsets and calls contentEncoding with the request Content-Type header before writing StatusUnsupportedMediaType.

evidenceNotes.claim: Existing ContentCharset tests cover only unquoted charset parameter values.
evidenceNotes.evidence: TestContentCharset table cases use charset=UTF-8, charset=utf-8, and charset=Latin-1 without any quoted parameter variant.

evidenceNotes.claim: The middleware test file is the in-repository consumer of the exported ContentCharset API.
evidenceNotes.evidence: TestContentCharset installs the middleware with r.Use(ContentCharset(tt.inputContentCharset...)) and asserts the resulting HTTP status.

evidenceNotes.claim: The split helper is the concrete parsing primitive used for charset extraction in the pinned snapshot.
evidenceNotes.evidence: split uses strings.Cut and strings.TrimSpace to return two trimmed parts and is called twice by contentEncoding.

evidenceNotes.claim: AllowContentType is not materially affected because it ignores media parameters entirely.
evidenceNotes.evidence: AllowContentType cuts the Content-Type header at the first ';' and compares only the media type, so quoted charset values cannot alter its result.

evidenceNotes.claim: Switching to a standards-based media type parser can change outcomes for malformed headers.
evidenceNotes.evidence: The current split-based code accepts arbitrary text after 'charset=', whereas a strict parser would report an error for malformed parameters.

evidenceNotes.claim: The exact parser and fallback semantics for malformed quoted parameters are not established by the base snapshot.
evidenceNotes.evidence: The pinned file contains only split-based extraction and no quoted-string handling, error fallback, or additional helper.
